intro.title: Discriminated Union Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays different types of notifications, such as success, warning, and error messages. You'll learn how to use discriminated union props, a pattern in TypeScript and JavaScript that helps ensure type safety by using a common property (like 'type') to distinguish between different possible shapes of props. The main technologies involved are React functional components, JSX for rendering, and conditional rendering based on the prop's discriminant. This approach makes your components more predictable and easier to maintain by clearly defining the data they can receive.
intro.usecase: Discriminated union props are essential for building robust, type-safe UI components that can render in multiple distinct states. For example, a dashboard card might display as a loading skeleton, an error message, or a data visualization—each requiring different props and structure. This pattern is commonly used in form steps, modals with different content types, or navigation menus with icon-only and text-and-icon variants, ensuring the component only receives valid props for its current mode.
